Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: USAFMCOM is a Major Subordinate Command to the U.S. Army Materiel Command (AMC) whose mission is to deliver logistics, sustainment and material readiness from the installation to the forward tactical edge to ensure globally dominant land force capabilities. USAFMCOM performs Army-wide and Army-unique actions such as financial management functions and financial support services. These include but are not limited to: financial systems support and sustainment; technical training; electronic commerce; classified finance and accounting; audit resolution strategies; standardization of financial business processes; functional sustainment to the General Funds Enterprise Business System (GFEBS) ERP, as well as liaison functions throughout the Army and Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS). USAFMCOM also provides technical coordination for Finance and Comptroller (FC) units and military pay support with commands across the Army, in order to ensure the effective implementation of policies and programs to support optimally resourcing the Army and supporting Soldiers.
MajorDuties: Plans and organizes work to be accomplished and establishes long range and short-term priorities. Assigns work to subordinate employees based on immediate priorities, workload, difficulty of assignments, and the capabilities of employees and reviews work for technical adequacy and compliance with established policies, procedures, and deadlines. Provides advice, guidance, and instruction to employees on both work and administrative matters. Responsible for process improvement through ongoing analysis of customer needs to increase work unit productivity and quality. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Qualifications: To qualify for an Accountant (Staff) your resume and supporting documentation must support: A. Basic Requirement: A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting. The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. Applicants MUST submit a copy of their college transcripts from an accredited educational institution which reflects that an accounting or equivalent degree was conferred and the date conferred. Failure to submit your transcripts may result in lost consideration. OR A combination of education and experience - at least 4 years of experience in accounting, or an equivalent combination of accounting experience, college-level education, and training that provided professional accounting knowledge. Applicants MUST submit a copy of their college transcripts from an accredited educational institution. Failure to submit your transcripts may result in lost consideration. The applicant's background must also include one of the following: Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality. This can include up to 6 hours of business law; A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; or Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; and (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements. AND B. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position, and is directly in or related to this position. In addition to meeting the Basic Requirement above, to qualify for the GS-13 grade level, specialized experience must be at the GS-12 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut-off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: Manage the internal control process within an organization, including identifying risks, developing control objectives and activities, performing tests of design and effectiveness, and, developing and implementing corrective action plans. Audit an organization's internal control program. Perform an examination or supporting the organization undergoing an examination in accordance with AICPA SSAE No. 18, Attestation Standards: Clarification and Recodification, § AT-C 320, "Reporting on an Examination of Controls at a Service Organization Relevant to User Entities' Internal Control Over Financial Reporting." Participate in an evaluation of System and Organization Controls (SOC) 1 Reports in accordance with AICPA Statement on Auditing Standard-Clarified (AU-C) § 402, "Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organization." Prepare reports or analyses as outputs and working with other organizations obtain their concurrences. Develop or implement business activities that streamlined these functions. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.Evaluations: The assessments for this job will measure the following Competencies: Concepts, Policies, and Principles of Finance Accounting Analysis Concepts, Policies and Principles of Audit Financial Stewardship Communication Accountability Arithmetic Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Flexibility Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Mathematical Reasoning Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork Once the application process is complete, we may review your résumé and supporting documents to ensure you meet the basic qualification requirements. We may evaluate each applicant who meets the basic qualifications on the information provided and evaluate your relevant personal, educational, and work experiences as it relates to fundamental competencies, identified in the Qualifications section above, required for this position. Based on the results of this evaluation, you will be placed in one of the following quality categories: Best-Qualified: This highest category will be used for those candidates who possess the type and quality of experience that substantially exceeds the minimum qualifications of the position, including all selective placement factors and appropriate quality ranking factor(s), as determined by the job analysis. Highly-Qualified: This higher category will be used for those candidates who possess the type and quality of experience that exceed the minimum qualifications of the position, as determined by the job analysis. Qualified: This lowest category will be used for those candidates that meet the minimum qualifications of the position and are proficient in some, but not all, of the requirements of the position. Candidates may require extensive training and/or orientation in order to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position. Names of the candidates in the Best-Qualified category will be sent first to the hiring manager for employment consideration. Applicants in other categories will be referred in accordance with category rating procedures. Veteran's Preference: If you are entitled to veteran's preference, you should indicate the type of veteran's preference you are claiming on your résumé. Your veteran's preference entitlement will be verified by the employing agency. Qualified veterans' preference eligibles with a service-connected disability of 10% or more will be listed at the top of the highest quality category depending on the position and grade level of the job. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army .Fort Bliss supports over 30,000 troops, and has undergone the largest post expansion in the Army. It is the home of the 1st Armored Division, FORSCOM deployable units, and has a full scope of base support elements. Ft Bliss plays a vital role in America's largest city on a U.S. International Border, El Paso, Texas. El Paso's climate is dry/sunny with mild winters and warm summers. MajorDuties: Oversee financial management support functions, (e.g., budget services, managerial accounting, acquisition planning, manpower, equipment, etc.), in support of resource management programs.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Time in Grade: For entry at the GS-11 level, status applicants must have served 52 weeks as a GS-09 or higher grade in the Federal Service. For entry at the GS-12 level, status applicants must have served 52 weeks as a GS-11 or higher grade in the Federal Service. Specialized Experience: For the GS-11, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service, or comparable in difficulty and responsibility to GS-09 if outside the Federal service. Specialized experience is defined as performing financial systems analysis in support of military pay and the mobilization / de-mobilization process; providing thorough knowledge of financial management principles as they relate to automated systems processing and finance operations. For the GS-12, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service, or comparable in difficulty and responsibility to GS-11 if outside the Federal service. Specialized experience is defined as performing military entitlement analysis and assisting in the design, development, and support of military pay operations and related organizations. Demonstrates substantive knowledge of financial management principles as they relate to automated systems processing and operations. Examples of specialized experience include: Planning and implementing operational improvements to large-scale financial operations, systems, policies, and procedures. Providing high-level financial systems expertise to senior leadership to help them carry out financial missions with allocated resources. In addition to meeting the specialized experience requirements, qualified applicants must also possess the quality of experience as it relates to how closely or to what extent an applicant's background, recency of experience, education, and training are relevant to the duties and responsibilities of the announced position. Candidates must clearly demonstrate the possession of knowledge, skills and abilities, or competencies necessary to successfully perform the work of the position at the appropriate level to be qualified for the position. Applicants must describe how their experience meets the competencies within the body of the resume. No separate statements addressing KSA's or competencies are required. Competencies: Communication, Concepts, Policies, and Principles of Finance, Decision Support, Financial Management Analysis, and Financial Management Systems Qualification and time-in-grade requirements must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: USAFMCOM is a Major Subordinate Command to the U.S. Army Materiel Command (AMC) whose mission is to deliver logistics, sustainment and material readiness from the installation to the forward tactical edge to ensure globally dominant land force capabilities. USAFMCOM performs Army-wide and Army-unique actions such as financial management functions and financial support services. These include but are not limited to: financial systems support and sustainment; technical training; electronic commerce; classified finance and accounting; audit resolution strategies; standardization of financial business processes; functional sustainment to the General Funds Enterprise Business System (GFEBS) ERP, as well as liaison functions throughout the Army and Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS). USAFMCOM also provides technical coordination for Finance and Comptroller (FC) units and military pay support with commands across the Army, in order to ensure the effective implementation of policies and programs to support optimally resourcing the Army and supporting Soldiers.
MajorDuties: Manages and directs the operations of Defense Military Pay Office (DMPO) which requires the development of policies and procedures unique to each command in an environment of constantly changing priorities and missions.
Analyze financial data and management information systems reports at all levels in support of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Execution System (PPBES) process.
Conducts analysis to determine the effectiveness of operations, compliance with established policies and procedures, reliability of records and reports, and validity of supporting documentation.
Develop statistical data that defines the problems and identifies the proper reporting requirements to include necessary system changes.

Exercises accountability/ leadership oversight of audits and operational reviews performed by the Internal Control and Quality Review untis to ensure correct execution of DoD guidance, policies, and procedures with respect to Military Pay Operations.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Reinstatement In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for an Accountant: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in accounting; or a degree in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting. The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Must include at least 4 years of experience in accounting, or an equivalent combination of accounting experience, college-level education, and training that provided professional accounting knowledge. The applicant's background must also include one of the following: (1) Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality. This can include up to 6 hours of business law; OR (2) A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; OR (3) Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; AND (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; AND (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements. NOTE: In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes reconciling, analyzing or validating accounting records; evaluating financial data to identify problems or unfavorable trends; and utilizing various automated accounting programs/systems to complete tasks. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Accounting Operations Financial Management Leadership Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-11).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: The Installation rests in the beautiful 'hill and lake' country of Central Texas between Killeen and Copperas Cove and is approximately 60 miles north of the capital city of Austin, 50 miles south of Waco, 160 miles south of Dallas, and 150 miles north of San Antonio. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serves as a professional accountant to include providing guidance on policy, advising on trends, performing joint reconciliation and accounting analysis.

Distributing and monitoring workload among lower-grade accountants and financial analysts in accordance with established workflow or job specialization in order to ensure timely accomplishment of the assigned mission.
Provides professional managerial accounting policy advice and assistance to III Corps, Major Subordinate Commands (MSCs), Installation Management Agency (IMA), program managers and tenant activities.
Provides management officials with professional accounting advice and assistance related to the impact of financial transactions and issues.
Plans work to be accomplished, sets priorities and prepares schedules for completion of work by section analysts.
Assigns work based on priorities, selective consideration of the difficulty and requirements of assignments and the capabilities of employees.
Identifies developmental and training needs of employees, and provides or arranges for training through Supervisor Staff Accountant.

Details.JobSummary: This National Guard position is for a Budget Analyst, Position Description Number T5153000 and is part of the JFHQ-G4 New Jersey Army National Guard. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current Army Cyber Excepted Service (CES) Employee Current Army Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) Employee Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current DoD Cyber Excepted Service (CES) Employee (non-Army) Current Permanent DoD Civilian Employee (non-Army) Applying to Cyber Excepted Service Positions Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Accountant: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in accounting; or a degree in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting. The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Must include at least 4 years of experience in accounting, or an equivalent combination of accounting experience, college-level education, and training that provided professional accounting knowledge. The applicant's background must also include one of the following: (1) Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality. This can include up to 6 hours of business law; OR (2) A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; OR (3) Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; AND (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; AND (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe one year of specialized experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Specialized experience would be demonstrated by interpreting Office of Management and Budget and Government Accounting Office directives; regulatory material and instructions from higher headquarters; generally accepted budgetary, programming, and accounting principles and practices; decisions of the Comptroller General and special authorities; and delegated exemptions to implement or define financial policies and procedures for organization and subordinate organizations; developing new, specialized, and individually designed procedures to handle unique requirements to general fund accounting applications (i.e. Operation and Maintenance (OMA), Army; Research, Development, Test and Evaluation (RDT&E); Operation and Maintenance Reserve; Operation and Maintenance National Guard, Other Procurement Army, and Military Construction (MCA), Army); planning, developing and implementing new technological systems to accomplish general fund accounting, cost accounting, fixed asset accounting including interface relationships with higher or subordinate organization systems; coordinating with managers to define deficiencies in financial structures, management policies, and procedures related to the financial effectiveness of operations to make change recommendations and improve practices. This position is in the Supervision/Management Work Category at the Senior Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is a DOD Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system position in the Excepted Service under 10 USC 1599f. Employees occupying CES positions are in the Excepted Service and must adhere to U.S. Code, Title 10, as well as Department of Defense Instruction 1400.25. This position is located at the U.S. Army Cyber Command, Fort Eisenhower, Georgia. This position will be filled on a permanent basis.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serve as Accounting and Information Systems Division Chief for the DCSCMP, U.S. Army (ARCYBER).
Manage, supervise, and provide technical direction of accounting and information systems utilized to control ARCYBER financial resources.

Review, analyze, and interpret legislation, appropriation language and Office of Management and Budget and Office of the Secretary of Defense directives pertaining to assigned accounting and information systems.

Collaborate with subordinate organizations to develop plans, policies, procedures, review and analysis and reporting requirements, justification requirements, and technical guidance for assigned accounting functions.
Utilize a wide range of government laws, regulations, policies and procedures to implement and define local requirements.
Develop, recommend, and provide staff guidance concerning the overall accounting systems, diverse financial programs, and all appropriations for ARCYBER.

Plan, coordinate, and accomplish the development of procedures for implementation of ARCYBER accounting policy and for the functional design, development, application, and improvement of systems and procedures.
Provide guidance and technical assistance to officials in financial and managerial accounting systems.
Plan, direct, coordinate, and evaluate the work of technical personnel engaged in advising operating officials of approved accounting programs.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position will serve as a Supervisory Budget Analyst located at the US Army Training and Doctrine Command (TRADOC), G-8, Fort Eustis, VA.. Fort Eustis, VA is located in Newport News, between historic Williamsburg and Virginia Beach. Surrounding areas include Hampton, Norfolk, Portsmouth, Chesapeake and Virginia Beach. The Hampton Roads/Tidewater area has all the conveniences of a big city with charm of small town and rural areas.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Accountant (Staff): A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in accounting; or a degree in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting. The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Must include at least 4 years of experience in accounting, or an equivalent combination of accounting experience, college-level education, and training that provided professional accounting knowledge. The applicant's background must also include one of the following: (1) Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality. This can include up to 6 hours of business law; OR (2) A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; OR(3) Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; AND (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; AND (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements.In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Serialized Experience: To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe at least one year of specialized experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Specialized experience would be demonstrated by experience in using automated financial systems; creating and analyzing reports (for example: SAP programs/products); applying accounting, audit and inspection concepts(for example: General Ledger); identifying, researching, and resolving accounting system errors and Abnormal Balances; AND using Microsoft products (Excel, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, etc.) to create reports, briefs, and products for decision making. OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Accounting. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Are you interested in helping to defend our Nation? Exciting career opportunities are available with the U.S. Army Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM)! Fort Huachuca is located in Sierra Vista in Cochise County, in southeast Arizona, about 15 miles north of the border with Mexico. Sierra Vista enjoys an average year-round temperature of 74 degrees. A small community, with many amenities you would find in a larger city. Within a short driving distance are the mining towns of Bisbee and Tombstone, the "Town Too Tough to Die."; In addition to local and Tucson stores, shoppers also frequent Nogales, Naco, and Agua Prieta, Mexico, all within an hour-and-a-half drive from the post.
MajorDuties: Provides analysis of accounting reports and professional accounting advice on the status of funds and accounting trends, program and budget objectives, and policy requirements.
Advise management on the effects of proposed accounting or reporting changes, and on policies and procedures for improving financial management.
Participate in executing the financial processes for Funds Control Module (FCM) and the Global Combat Support System - Army (GCSS-A) for NETCOM.

Serve as lead accountant for FCM and GCSS-A to identify erroneous accounting transactions, determining necessary corrective action, coordinating with responsible action officers, and ensuring necessary action is taken on a timely and accurate basis.
Participate in ensuring the soundness of the command's direct reported financial data for all appropriations.
Provide support to other managerial accountants in STAMIS to include the General Fund Enterprise Business System (GFEBS), Wide Area Workflow (WAWF).
Act as the liaison between the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) Field Sites and the command's program managers.
Serve as primary action officer on Government Travel Card Inquiry System (EAGLS) and as Activity Program Coordinator (APC) for all civilian and military assigned to HQ NETCOM.

MajorDuties: Develop and formulate assigned segment(s) of the Command Operating Budget (COB) request for the current fiscal year plus two.

Review and analyze budget estimates submitted by assigned major activities and other staff elements for regulatory compliance, justification relative to objectives, previous obligation experience, and other pertinent factors.
Develop schedules for inclusion in COB submission to higher headquarters. Write and/or edit narrative statements justifying activity funding requests.
Use a variety of personal computer-based software programs, including spreadsheets and data bases, to develop analytical techniques for the purpose of budget formulation, execution, and analysis.
Review budgetary transactions to determine whether obligations, expenditures, and requested allotments are within funding limitations in the approved budget.
Use automated accounting and budget systems to reconcile transactions, correct errors, and generate automated financial reports.
Develop annual funding program and prepare quarterly funding documents issued to major activities and other staff elements.
Develop revisions to funding programs; make minor and/or recommend major reprogramming to shift funds in areas where additional dollar resources are needed.
Perform an in-depth, rigorous analysis of budget requests, budget execution, and actual costs by employing cost-effective analysis, program trade-off, and exploring alternative methods of funding.
Review and analyze program costs and obligations, performance forecasts and reports, financial reports, and other documentation.
Prepare a variety of reports covering the status of funds, and obligations as required by higher headquarters. Responsible for month-end and year-end close-out.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Fort Irwin is a world class training center for America's Soldiers, known for its excellent desert training and vast recreational opportunities. Located 37 miles NE of Barstow, CA, in the Mojave Desert midway between Las Vegas, NV and Los Angeles, CA. Nearest airports are in Ontario, CA (120 miles), Los Angeles (175 miles) and Las Vegas (180 miles). Fort Irwin has a mass bus system that travels to and from Barstow (37 miles) and Victorville (69 miles). For information on these cities, visit their websites: http://www.barstowca.org/; http://www.losangeles.com/; http://ci.victorville.ca.us/; https://www.ontarioca.gov/; http://www.lasvegasnevada.gov/. Fort Irwin is one of the 4th highest paying federal installations, falling under the Los Angeles-Long Beach, CA locality at 34.89%. Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Responsible for planning, scheduling, and coordinating the efforts of the garrison budget, to produce a budget plan and execution process for the organization and supported garrison activities.

Serves as a financial consultant on issues such as: budgeting strategies and techniques; use of financial management products; financial forecasts and projections; and development of annual and long-range financial plans.
Performs a wide range of administrative, technical, and analytical duties in the formulation, presentation, defense, and execution of the garrison's budget.
Develops, and/or assists managers in developing, extensive written justification in support of these budget requirements.
Presents and defends the garrison's budget estimates to fund reviewing and granting authorities in higher headquarters.

Reviews and validates obligations, expenditures, reimbursable orders, requests for allotments, etc. by examining accounting records, through continuing dialogue with program officials and their staffs, and by reviewing financial documents.

Plans work to be accomplished by budget analyst and supporting personnel, setting priorities and scheduling completion. Assigns work based on priorities and selective considerations of the difficulty of assignments and capabilities of personnel.

QUALIFICATIONS FOR GS-07: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes assisting with routine and recurring budget administrative duties such as compiling budgetary data to compose reports; checking budgetary records to determine availability of funds; and maintaining budgetary records for currency, accuracy, and compliance with regulations. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). -OR- Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Accounting, Finance, etc. (NOTE: You MUST submit copies of ALL your transcripts.) -OR- Superior Academic Achievement: Successful completion of all the requirements for a bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement. In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled. Superior Academic Achievement is based on:(1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses. (NOTE: You MUST submit copies of ALL your transcripts.) -OR- (2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum. (NOTE: You MUST submit copies of ALL your transcripts.) -OR- (3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/). (NOTE: You MUST submit copies of ALL your transcripts.) -OR- Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages. (NOTE: You MUST submit copies of ALL your transcripts.) QUALIFICATIONS FOR GS-09: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes tracking funding requirements; assisting in compiling financial information for budget reports; and researching obligation discrepancies to assist in recommending corrective action. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). -OR- Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree -in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Accounting, Finance, etc. (NOTE: You MUST submit copies of ALL your transcripts.) -OR- Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. (NOTE: You MUST submit copies of ALL your transcripts.) You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Accountability Arithmetic/Mathematical Reasoning Attention to Detail Budget Administration Communications Contracting/Procurement Customer Service Decision Making Financial Systems Flexibility Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork Time in Grade Requirement for GS-7: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-05). Time in Grade Requirement for GS-9: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-07). NOTE: Applicants must meet all Time-in-Grade requirements and experience requirements within 30 days of the closing date of the announcement. Current employees applying under VEOA are subject to time-in-grade restrictions like any other GS employee. Please see the specific instructions regarding supporting documentation for Time in Grade requirements in the REQUIRED DOCUMENTS section, below.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Fort Leavenworth is located in the Greater Kansas City metropolitan area. The immediate area is considered a national treasure with historic sites and homes filled with small-town charm and friendliness merged with Kansas City retail, attractions and entertainment. Kansas City, well known for its BBQ, Jazz and fountains, is rich in culture with a thriving performing arts scene. Honored as one of the World's 15 Most Beautiful Concert Halls, the Kauffman Center attracts some of the world's most renowned performers and entertainers. For the sports enthusiasts, Kansas City hosts professional sports with the Royals, Chiefs and Sporting Kansas City soccer club. An international airport is conveniently located within a 30 minute drive of Fort Leavenworth. More information may be found at www.visitkc.com or https://garrison.leavenworth.army.mil
MajorDuties: At the developmental level (GS-07), you will perform assignments under closer than normal supervision. The full performance level (GS-09) entails the following duties which is not an all-inclusive list:
Verify that commitment and obligation documents are properly prepared and have the required supporting schedules and approvals.

Verify that cost estimates are reasonable and reflect all known costs by verifying air fares with the Transportation Office, equipment or supply costs with Procurement, and per diem rates with Finance and Accounting.
Ensure that commitments are entered timely and accurately in the automated accounting system.
Use statistical methods to show current execution percentages and serve as the basis for projecting future actions.
Write analyses to be used to brief the supervisor on funding status.
Gather data, performs analysis, and completes schedules for a variety of official reporting requirements.
Maintain automated commitment records for assigned Program Directors/key accounts.

Basic Requirements Degree: accounting; or a degree in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting. The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. (The term "accounting" means "accounting and/or auditing" in this standard. The applicant's background must also include one of the following: Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality. This can include up to 6 hours of business law; A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; or Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; and (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Position is with the US Army MSCoE G8 OFFICE, ACCOUNTING DIVISON at Ft. Leonard Wood, MO. Located in the beautiful South-Central Missouri Ozarks. It covers more than 61,000 acres and is located in Pulaski County, MO. Bordering the installation to the North are the towns of Waynesville/St. Robert and Interstate 44. St. Louis is a 2-hour drive to the East along I-44 and Springfield is a little more than an hour's drive to the West of Ft. Leonard Wood.

MajorDuties: As Chief of the Managerial Accounting Division, serves as the installation's accountant, responsible for the continuing review, revision, improvement, and adjustment of the entire appropriated financial accounting program at the installation.
Issues appropriate directive/ guidance, directs actions to be taken, and resolves procedural problems.
Provides meaningful information to managers regarding the effectiveness and efficiency of their financial management systems and practices.

Reviews and analyzes a wide variety of documents, reports, policies, operations, and procedures at installation-wide level. Develops alternative options, to assist managers in improving financial management performance.
Serves as a systems accountant to perform professional accounting work.

Applies considerable ingenuity to solve a wide variety of complex systems problems where no clear precedents exist. Work may involve continuing study and revision of an existing system or design of subsystems. Identifies financial trends.

Identifies and resolves problems in accounting reports through analysis of reports, which are used by management to preclude budget activities from violating the Anti Deficiency Act and to monitor financial trends to ensure optimum use of resources.

Activities are notified through verbal and written communication of the trends identified with recommended changes to revise unfavorable trends. Accounting problems are reviewed and resolved by incumbent.

Participates in management decision-making by providing assistance in interpreting and applying financial data and information, in developing suggestions, alternatives, and recommendations which contribute to the decision making process.
Suggests approaches to be taken and in using accounting data to more effectively manage programs.
Supervises activities and employees involved in the application or accounting principles, theories, concepts and practices to a wide variety, of difficult problems.
Keeps employees informed of management goals and objectives.

Responsible for personnel management to include recruitment, selection, evaluation of performance, action on leave requests, awards, initiation of disciplinary actions, and all other necessary functions.
Plans work to be accomplished by subordinates.
Establishes standards of performance and evaluates subordinates performance.
Provides advice, counsel, or instruction to individual employees involving technical, work as, well as administrative matters.
Interviews candidates for selection, promotion and/or reassignment, within area of responsibility.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is with the United States Army Civil Affairs and Psychological Operations Command, Comptroller Branch, G-8, located at Fort LIberty, North Carolina.
Details.SubAgencyName: United States Army Civil Affairs and Psychological Operations Command
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Monitor the status of resources to ensure the Command budget is appropriately integrated.
Review fund utilizations to handle unexpected occurrences.
Analyze proposals to determine if the requested funds are available.
Utilize web-based resource planning systems to track and analyze budget information.
Formulate the annual budget to ensure the organization's priorities are funded.
Modify the operating program to be consistent with the approved budget.
Prepare budget estimates for management to plan expenditures.
Utilize budgeting techniques, such as linear regression models, cost-benefit analysis, standard deviation formulas, or activity based costing to revise budget estimates.
Ensure that adequate control systems are developed to monitor the annual budget.
Follow organizational guidelines and limitations to execute the annual budget.
Prepare monthly status reports for management to track the annual budget.
Prepare budget proposals to submit to headquarters for approval.
Formulate budget guidance to ensure compliance with rules and regulations.
Ensure the organization's priorities are properly stated in budget estimates.
Provide administrative guidance to Command staff to carry out budget functions.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is with the United States Army Civil Affairs and Psychological Operations Command, Comptroller Branch, G-8, located at Fort Liberty, North Carolina.
Details.SubAgencyName: United States Army Civil Affairs and Psychological Operations Command
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. Review fund utilizations to handle unexpected occurrences.

Formulate the annual budget to ensure the organization's priorities are funded.

Prepare budget proposals to submit to headquarters for approval.
Formulate budget guidance to ensure compliance with rules and regulations.
Ensure the organization's priorities are properly stated in budget estimates.
Provide administrative guidance to Command staff to carry out budget functions.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. GS-05: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes work that involves Performing progressively responsible financial, accounting, clerical, and/or office administration work; Reviewing, determining, processing and/or resolving recurring administrative problems; Researching and interpreting regulations; Reviewing information to respond to recurring written and verbal inquires. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-04). OR Education: Four years of education above the high school level obtained in an accredited business, secretarial or technical school, junior college, college or university. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of education beyond two years (total semester hours minus 60) by 60. Add the two percentages. GS-06 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes work that involves Using a wide variety of military pay regulations, requirements, procedures, and operations to review and process routine military pay actions; Using automated pay systems to process military pay actions; Providing customer service by answering written and telephonic military pay inquires. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. GS-07 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes work that involves Utilizing a variety of pay regulations, requirements, procedures, and operations to review and determine eligibility for military pay actions; Using automated pay systems to process military pay actions; Researching and making necessary corrections associated with erroneous military pay actions; and Processing non-routine pay adjustments such as special entitlements, special pay, indebtedness or under payments. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-06). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted.

Details.JobSummary: This is a Direct Hire Authority (DHA) solicitation utilizing the DHA for Financial Management Experts to recruit and appoint qualified candidates to positions in the competitive service. About the Position: This position is with the United States Army Reserve Command G-8, United States Army Reserve Pay Management Division, Reserve Military Pay Branch located at Fort McCoy, Wisconsin.
Details.SubAgencyName: G-8, Pay Management Division, Reserve Military Pay Branch
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Perform comprehensive review of master military pay account transactions for Army Reserve service members ensuring compliance with policies, pay entitlement laws, regulations, precedent decisions and procedures.
Research current and prior pay regulations, laws, and guidance to resolve complex pay actions.

Resolve complex military reserve pay cases such as under/over payments, leave and separation adjustments, bonus eligibility, combat zone special pay, locality pay, overseas entitlements, hazardous duty pay, severance pay, and incapacitation pay.
Review system output and error reports to determine cause, trends, and other statistical information.

Analyze problems, advisories, and reject messages relating to an automated military pay application, the Defense Joint Military Pay Systems Reserve Components (DJMS-RC), Defense Military Office (DMO).
Utilize military automated systems to create, review and audit military reserve pay transactions.

Provide military entitlements, pay, and benefits technical guidance and direct service support to deployed and non-deployed Soldiers, units, Reserve Personnel Action Centers, Readiness Divisions, and Army Finance Officers.
Provide technical support to Army Finance offices on processing entitlement and administrative actions for deployed United States Army Reserve (USAR) Soldiers.

GS-05: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes work that involves Performing progressively responsible financial, accounting, clerical, and/or office administration work; Reviewing, determining, processing and/or resolving recurring administrative problems; Researching and interpreting regulations; Reviewing information to respond to recurring written and verbal inquires. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-04). OR Education: Four years of education above the high school level obtained in an accredited business, secretarial or technical school, junior college, college or university. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of education beyond two years (total semester hours minus 60) by 60. Add the two percentages. GS-06 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes work that involves Using a wide variety of military pay regulations, requirements, procedures, and operations to review and process routine military pay actions; Using automated pay systems to process military pay actions; Providing customer service by answering written and telephonic military pay inquires. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this grade, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. GS-07 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes work that involves Utilizing a variety of pay regulations, requirements, procedures, and operations to review and determine eligibility for military pay actions; Using automated pay systems to process military pay actions; Researching and making necessary corrections associated with erroneous military pay actions; and Processing non-routine pay adjustments such as special entitlements, special pay, indebtedness or under payments. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-06). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this grade, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is with the United States Army Reserve Command G-8, United States Army Reserve Pay Management Division, Reserve Military Pay Branch located at Fort McCoy, Wisconsin. May be selected at GS-05, GS-06, or GS-07 level. This is a developmental position up to full performance level, GS-07. Noncompetitive promotion to the full performance level authorized.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Perform comprehensive review of master military pay account transactions for Army Reserve service members ensuring compliance with policies, pay entitlement laws, regulations, precedent decisions and procedures.
Research current and prior pay regulations, laws, and guidance to resolve complex pay actions.

Resolve complex military reserve pay cases such as under/over payments, leave and separation adjustments, bonus eligibility, combat zone special pay, locality pay, overseas entitlements, hazardous duty pay, severance pay, and incapacitation pay.
Review system output and error reports to determine cause, trends, and other statistical information.

Analyze problems, advisories, and reject messages relating to an automated military pay application, the Defense Joint Military Pay Systems Reserve Components (DJMS-RC), Defense Military Office (DMO).
Utilize military automated systems to create, review and audit military reserve pay transactions.

Provide military entitlements, pay, and benefits technical guidance and direct service support to deployed and non-deployed Soldiers, units, Reserve Personnel Action Centers, Readiness Divisions, and Army Finance Officers.
Provide technical support to Army Finance offices on processing entitlement and administrative actions for deployed United States Army Reserve (USAR) Soldiers.

Details.JobSummary: National Defense University (NDU) supports the joint warfighter by providing rigorous Joint Professional Military Education to members of the U.S. Armed Forces and select others in order to develop leaders who have the ability to operate and creatively think in an unpredictable and complex world. This position is being filled under the Direct Hire Authority for Certain Personnel of the Department of Defense via delegated authority by the Office of the Secretary of Defense.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: National Defense University (NDU) is the premier national security institution focused on advanced joint education, leader development and scholarship. Under the direction and leadership of the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the oversight of the Director for Joint Force Development, Joint Staff (J-7), NDU offers a collegial and collaborative academic environment to support the joint warfighter by providing rigorous Joint Professional Military Education (JPME) and other graduate level programs to members of the U.S. Armed Forces and select others in order to develop leaders who have the ability to operate and creatively think in an unpredictable and complex world. NDU is comprised of five primary educational institutions and four additional component agencies: National War College (NWC), Dwight Eisenhower School (ES), Joint Forces Staff College (JFSC), College of International Security Affairs (CISA), the College of Information and Cyberspace (CIC), Institute for National Strategic Studies (INSS), International Student Management Office, Operations Support and the CAPSTONE General and Flag Officer Course. NDU has a comprehensive benefits package that includes retirement, social security, and thrift savings plan (TSP); health, life, and long-term care insurance; paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays. NDU employees enjoy flexible work schedules, transit subsidy and enhanced telework opportunities.
MajorDuties: Responsible for the administration of the Risk Management and Internal Controls (RMIC) program. Provides oversight of assessable units and assessable unit managers, who are responsible for assessing internal controls in their respective areas.

Serves as an expert advisor to supervisors, senior managers and colleagues in all areas of professional accounting, auditing and business controls. Establishes and audits accounting programs, academic and business processes in support of NDU mission.
Conducts audits of budgetary reports and financial statements utilizing in-depth understanding of, and familiarity with, generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).
Serves as the NDU entry point of contact for audit inquiries from the Department of Defense Inspector General (DoDIG), Government Accountability Office (GAO) and other investigative organizations.

Develops criteria for internal assessment topics for evaluation based on Secretary of Defense and Joint Staff priority areas, DoD management guidelines and NDU leadership priorities. Performs other duties as assigned.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Department of Defense Education Activity (DoDEA), as one of only two Federally-operated school systems, is responsible for planning, directing, coordinating, and managing prekindergarten through 12th grade educational programs on behalf of the Department of Defense (DoD). DoDEA is globally positioned, operating 160 accredited schools in 8 districts located in 11 foreign countries, 7 states, Guam, and Puerto Rico. DoDEA employs approximately 15,000 employees who serve more than 72,000 children of active duty military and DoD civilian families. DoDEA is committed to ensuring that all school-aged children of military families are provided a world-class education that prepares them for postsecondary education and/or career success and to be leading contributors in their communities as well as in our 21st century globalized society.

Utilizing agency developed programs to submit budget data to headquarters for approval.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located in Fort Moore, Georgia within the DoDEA Headquarters RM Support Branch.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Department of Defense Education Activity (DoDEA), as one of only two Federally-operated school systems, is responsible for planning, directing, coordinating, and managing prekindergarten through 12th grade educational programs on behalf of the Department of Defense (DoD). DoDEA is globally positioned, operating 160 accredited schools in 8 districts located in 11 foreign countries, 7 states, Guam, and Puerto Rico. DoDEA employs approximately 15,000 employees who serve more than 72,000 children of active duty military and DoD civilian families. DoDEA is committed to ensuring that all school-aged children of military families are provided a world-class education that prepares them for postsecondary education and/or career success and to be leading contributors in their communities as well as in our 21st century globalized society.
MajorDuties: Analyzing budget execution to recommend and verify appropriate use of resources.
Monitoring the execution of approved operating budget to assure funds are properly obligated.
Reviewing budget estimates to identify imbalances and duplicates.
Advising personnel and administrators on budgetary and financial matters.
Maintaining organizational processes to safeguard funds, properties and costs and obligations against fraud, waste and abuse.
Conducting briefings and formal training on a variety of finance related topics to inform employees, management and officials on current policy and procedures.
Coordinating with other local agencies or military commands to review Interservice Support Agreements (ISA), or like agreements or categories of billings for integrity, accuracy and propriety.
Utilizing agency developed programs to submit budget data to headquarters for approval.

Candidates in this category meet the minimum experience requirements for the announced position.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Time in Grade: For entry at the GS-07 level, status applicants must have served 52 weeks as a GS-06 or higher grade in the Federal Service.For entry at the GS-08 level, status applicants must have served 52 weeks as a GS-07 or higher grade in the Federal Service. Specialized Experience:You must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to the next lower grade level in the Federal service. For the GS -7: Specialized experience is defined as reviewing and processing a wide variety of non-recurring military payroll transactions; determining entitlements; verifying all documents for propriety, completeness and accuracy; and resolving problems within automated pay accounts related to payroll actions, regulations, policies and procedures. For the GS -8: Specialized experience is defined as Investigating, resolving and/or identifying problems, errors and discrepancies within an automated military pay system; and reconstructing complex military pay histories to resolve pay and entitlements errors. In addition to meeting the specialized experience requirements, qualified applicants must also possess the quality of experience as it relates to how closely or to what extent an applicant's background, recency of experience, education, and training are relevant to the duties and responsibilities of the announced position. Candidates must clearly demonstrate the possession of knowledge, skills and abilities, or competencies necessary to successfully perform the work of the position at the appropriate level to be qualified for the position. Applicants must describe how their experience meets the competencies within the body of the resume. No separate statements addressing KSA's or competencies are required. Competencies: Communication, Concepts, Policies, and Principles of Payroll, Financial Management Systems, Fundamentals and Operations of Military and Civilian Pay, and Leading People Qualification and time-in-grade requirements must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: This position with USAFMCOM is located at Ft. Moore, GA. This announcement will be used to fill positions with an entry grade of GS-8, or GS-7 with a target grade of GS-8.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: USAFMCOM is a Major Subordinate Command to the U.S. Army Materiel Command (AMC) whose mission is to deliver logistics, sustainment and material readiness from the installation to the forward tactical edge to ensure globally dominant land force capabilities. USAFMCOM performs Army-wide and Army-unique actions such as financial management functions and financial support services. These include but are not limited to: financial systems support and sustainment; technical training; electronic commerce; classified finance and accounting; audit resolution strategies; standardization of financial business processes; functional sustainment to the General Funds Enterprise Business System (GFEBS) ERP, as well as liaison functions throughout the Army and Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS). USAFMCOM also provides technical coordination for Finance and Comptroller (FC) units and military pay support with commands across the Army, in order to ensure the effective implementation of policies and programs to support optimally resourcing the Army and supporting Soldiers.
MajorDuties: Serves as a Lead Military Pay Technician responsible for providing instructions, distributing and balancing the workload of three or more employees who perform such work as processing a wide variety of military pay transactions.

Distributes and balances the workload among employees in accordance with established work flow or job specialization, assures timely accomplishment of the assigned workload, and assures that each employee has enough work to keep busy.
Keeps in touch with the status and progress of work, and makes day-to-day adjustments in accordance with established priorities, obtaining assistance from the supervisor on problems that may arise.
Estimates and reports on expected time of completion of work and maintains records of work accomplishments and time expended and prepares production reports as request.
Instructs employees on tasks and job requirements, develops written instruction as necessary, and answers questions regarding procedures, policies, and directives.
Reviews a full range of technician transactions to determine correct input; returns or rejects work for corrective action.

The view this policy, please copy and paste the following web address into your web browser: http://www.dtic.mil/whs/directives/corres/pdf/1400.25-V300.pdf. This position is subject to the limitations imposed by the DOD Priority Placement Program. PPP Application Based Preference Eligibles (Military Reserve and National Guard technicians, Military Reserve and National Guard technicians receiving disability retirement, and Retained Grade employees) will receive priority consideration at the full performance level only. For grades below the full performance level, only MSP/PPP eligible candidates who currently occupy a formal training program position will be entitled to exercise their priority preference.
